transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay, um, good morning everyone. Can everyone hear me? Great. So welcome to the kick-off for the remote control project.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Morning. Yeah, I can hear you fine.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Morning, sorry, just getting the laptop to, um, connect to the projector.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: No worries, we've got time.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: So I'm Sam, I'm the project manager. Priya you're industrial design, Leo is user interface, and Hannah is marketing. Right?

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: That's right.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay so the agenda today is, uh, getting to know each other, then the project plan, then we'll talk about the budget and, um, how we split up the next phase.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Did anyone watch the match last night by the way?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Oh don't, I'm still annoyed about the second half.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Ha, yeah, let's, let's keep that for the coffee break. So. The client wants a new remote control for televisions. Original, trendy and user friendly.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Trendy, okay. That's, that's quite vague.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: It is a bit vague, which is why the marketing input matters. Hannah?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yeah so I had a quick look. Um, the main thing is that people say they hate how many buttons their remote has. Like, most of them use maybe five buttons.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Mm-hmm. That matches what I see. Channel, volume, power, and then, yeah, basically nothing.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: So fewer buttons. That makes my life easier actually, for the casing.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: And the younger market, the sixteen to thirty-five group, they care about how it looks. They want it to look fancy, like a gadget.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: So are we agreed we're going after the younger market with a fancy look and feel?

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Yeah, I'm fine with that.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Yeah. Agreed.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yes, that's the data.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay good, so that's decided, younger market, fancy look and feel. Let's write that down.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Should it control just the television or, um, also the DVD player and so on?

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Good question. Hannah, what does the research say?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Um, the universal ones are, they're bigger and they cost more, and the clients' brief just says television.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: And a universal remote has all those extra modes, which is, which is exactly the many-buttons problem.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Right. So just the TV. Single device. Everybody okay with that?

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Fine by me.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Yeah. Single device.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay, decision made, single-device TV remote.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: What's the budget, do we know?

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Yes, so the production cost has to be under, um, twelve fifty euros per unit. Twelve and a half. And the selling price is twice that.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Twelve fifty. Okay. That's tight if we do anything with, like, a fancy material.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Plastic with a rubber coating is cheap though.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, that might work.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: So that's the budget, twelve fifty. It is fixed, we go with that.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Hang on, have we thought about, like, maybe we should look into speech recognition? Like you shout at it to find the remote. Everyone's got a phone that does voice.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Ha, that's the find-my-remote thing. That would be cool.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: It would add, uh, a microphone and a chip. Not under twelve fifty I think.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yeah no, I just, I don't know, maybe worth a look at some point.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Let's park that. Nobody is taking it on right now but it's a fair idea, we can revisit.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: If we had the money, we could do a touch screen, but, you know, if we had the money.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: If we had the money I'd have a different job.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Ha.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay. Let's move on to who does what. For the next phase, we each go away and work on our own thing individually. Priya, you'd do the working design.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Yeah, I can do that. I'll draft a sketch of the casing, like rough shapes and materials, and get it to you all by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: This Friday, the sixth?

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Yes, Friday the sixth.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Great. Leo?

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: So I will, um, I'll try to look at the interface, like the minimum button layout. I'm a bit swamped with the other project though, so, I'll try, but I can't promise it's done.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay, noted. Hannah, you have the market research already.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Right. I'll send you all the summary of it. Wednesday okay? I just need to tidy up the charts.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Wednesday the fourth, perfect.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: And I'll write up the minutes and email them out after this, today.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Thanks Sam.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Oh, one thing. Batteries. Who's going to talk to the battery supplier? Because the type of battery changes the thickness of the whole thing.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Hmm. Good point. I don't know. Who, who is going to do that?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Not me, I don't have contacts with the, with the hardware people.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Don't look at me.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: I mean, it affects me most, but I haven't got the account.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Okay, so that's open. We'll sort out who does it next meeting.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitaker
transcript.text: Anything else? No? Okay, so, um, thank you all, this was a good start.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Cole
transcript.text: Thanks. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Leo Brandt
transcript.text: Bye all.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: See you.

decisions.text: The remote will target a younger market with a fancy look and feel
The remote control will be a single-device TV remote, not a universal one
Production budget is twelve and a half euros per unit
